lockedFacts: HRRR is an operational NOAA high-resolution numerical weather model with approximately 3 km horizontal grid spacing over the contiguous United States
NOAA describes the model as predicting the atmosphere at 50 vertical elevations above each horizontal grid point
limits: cloud-resolving/high-resolution model language does not make HRRR grid state an observation of every local cloud structure
3 km support remains much coarser than close-range cinematic/realtime volume footprints

lockedFacts: CONUS native-level HRRR products are listed at 3 km Lambert Conformal resolution
the native-level analysis inventory contains 50 hybrid levels

native hybrid levels expose pressure, cloud liquid mixing ratio CLWMR, cloud ice mixing ratio CIMIXR, cloud-droplet number concentration NCONCD, cloud-ice number concentration NCCICE, cloud fraction FRACCC, geopotential height HGT, temperature TMP and specific humidity SPFH among other fields
the HRRR sub-hourly product is explicitly a 2-D Surface Levels product; the product page says each file contains the forecast hour plus 15, 30 and 45 minutes before the hour
the listed sub-hourly analysis inventory contains surface/column/cloud-base/cloud-top/radiation diagnostics rather than a 50-level native microphysics state
limits: product inventories describe model output schema, not observed atmospheric truth
absence of renderer-specific extinction/scattering/albedo/phase quantities means a separate optical closure is still required
the inventory page warns actual parameters may differ from those listed; live indexes should be checked for executable ingestion

lockedFacts: the official NOMADS directory exposed HRRR data for 2026-09-09 when checked
the 2026-09-09 00 UTC CONUS native analysis file hrrr.t00z.wrfnatf00.grib2 was listed at approximately 667 MB and its index at approximately 59 KB
the live index records d=2026090900 and repeats CLWMR/CIMIXR/NCONCD/NCCICE/FRACCC/HGT/PRES/TMP/SPFH through hybrid level 50
limits: the 667 MB file size is an operational sample, not a permanent size invariant
this cycle inspected directory/index metadata rather than decoding a selected GRIB2 value packet
whole-file browser ingestion is not implied or recommended; NOMADS exposes GRIB filtering and indexes suitable for subsetting

lockedFacts: NCEP production-status reporting showed HRRR hourly cycles completing in the current production suite around the R12 check
limits: operational status is time-varying and must be treated as lifecycle metadata rather than a Frozen source assumption

limits: RRFS transition status does not justify silently replacing HRRR in a current pipeline
